[DAY3 17:18:00 - DAY3 17:18:28]
I watch and study. Shure: "OK, this is fine, this is OK." "Alright, good," I say. I select the address. Alice: "You're not falling." I click on a few car models and request a taxi. Tasha: "Tired." I click to confirm. Lucia: "+1" Matching... "What? 10086, okay," I say. Alice: "10086." I look at my phone. Lucia: "Hahaha, 10036." I exit.

[DAY3 18:00:00 - DAY3 18:03:00]
During the car ride, I actively engaged with my phone and communicated with passengers to coordinate timing. I sat in the car, frequently checking my phone and opening relevant software, then called out to Lucia to check the time, showing the screen to Lucia, Shure, Tasha, and Katrina for confirmation. Noticing Alice in the back playing with her phone and feeling carsick, I continued using WeChat to manage messages despite the car’s movement, while occasionally looking out the window. This sequence reflects my multitasking to maintain communication and coordination during transit.

[DAY3 17:30:00 - DAY3 17:40:00]
The group navigates through a non-motorized lane. Initially, Shure points out that driving is not allowed in this area, and Tasha insists they can move through despite the narrow space. The group considers taking photos, with Tasha cautioning about the camera while squeezing through. I suggest walking as a viable option, and we attempt to move forward with Katrina leading.

I verify our location using a phone map. As the group continues along a bustling street, I ensure we are on the right path by checking the map and discuss with Lucia to select a suitable route. Tasha and I identify the correct car, a brown Buick with the number 776, waiting by the roadside. We confirm it's the right car and begin boarding.

We prepare to depart in the car. Tasha, Katrina, and I organize ourselves and our belongings inside, discussing the lack of trunk space. The group settles in, with me adjusting my personal items and preparing for the journey. Lucia suggests handling security measures, and I agree as the trip begins. Shure mentions not recording, and I instruct to start recording later. I express frustration at the trip's perceived pointlessness.
